text:
maya.s: Auditor asked for a tight evidence bundle for SOC2 + ISO: RBAC change on 2026-02-15, KMS key rotation metadata, and the post-triage notes for the CVE-2025-31415 vuln. Can we scope this to the minimal artifacts?
ashish.k: Yep. We should include: the rolebinding diff, admin approval email thread id (redacted emails), KMS key version list + access events around the rotation, and the incident ticket with triage notes.
sam.oncall: @ashish.k I can pull the RBAC diff from the cluster. Command I’ll run: ```kubectl get clusterrolebinding rbac-prod-edit -o yaml > /tmp/rbac-rprod-20260215.yaml``` then `git diff` against the deployment tag.
julia.ops: For KMS logs I’ll export a 48hr window (+ 7 days post-change) to a presigned S3 with 7d expiry. Will redact email addresses and replace with internal UID mapping. Anyone object? :lock:
auditor_jane: To be clear: we need proof of intent and proof of enforcement. Proof of intent = approval + planned change + who executed. Proof of enforcement = audit logs showing the change took effect and any policy alerts. Sampled logs are fine if we include full chain for the change itself.
ashish.k: Good point. I’ll attach the approval snippet (no PII) and the `kubectl apply` invocation from CI run. Example snippet I’ll include: ```-- apply manifest rbac/20260215-update.yaml -- user: actions-bot@redwood -- run_id: 98765```
lina.ciso: Also include the KMS key metadata: key id, creation/rotation timestamps, and IAM policy at time of rotation. Auditor will want to see the key wrapping event and which service account requested decrypt.
oncall-bot: Incident #INC-2026-42 linked: CVE-2025-31415 triage started 2026-02-14T18:05Z, mitigation PR merged 2026-02-15T02:11Z.
sam.oncall: I’ll add the incident ticket export (sanitized). For chain-of-custody we can provide a SHA256 manifest of every artifact in the bundle and a short note describing who pulled and when. Example: `manifest sha256sum: b1946ac92492d2347c6235b4d2611184`
julia.ops: Question for @auditor_jane — do you need full usernames or are pseudonymized UIDs acceptable for SOC2 evidence? We can provide a mapping under NDA if required.
auditor_jane: Pseudonymized UIDs are acceptable for the initial package. If we need to validate identity later, we’ll request the mapping via secure upload under the engagement.
maya.s: Ok action items: @sam.oncall export RBAC yaml + diff; @ashish.k gather approval snippet and CI run; @julia.ops export KMS events + IAM policy; @lina.ciso produce manifest + chain-of-custody statement. I'll assemble and upload to secure-share and post the presigned link here when ready. ETA EOD PST. :white_check_mark:
ashish.k: Noted. I’ll redact emails but keep raw actor ids in the artifact metadata.
sam.oncall: Export started — will post link when upload completes.
julia.ops: KMS export queued, will include `gcloud logging read` command in the notes for reproducibility.
lina.ciso: Remember to timestamp everything and include the evidence packaging checklist (signed by security lead).
maya.s: Thanks team — if anything blocks, ping me or escalate to oncall.
oncall-bot: Upload complete: https://secure-share.redwood/s/abcd1234 (expires 2026-03-03).
